product: Sealed 100 g plain Japanese steamed/dried Camellia sinensis sencha, paid personal postal shipment; no permits/certificates/special registrations/advance approvals; ordinary customs/arrival declarations allowed
conclusion: No destination closed. A valid published general processing exemption or exhaustive operative commodity list would suffice; unnamed tea does not automatically require a bespoke NPPO ruling. The reviewed material instead leaves specific category/list gaps. Access failures do not establish either prohibition or permission.

countries.reviewedBasis: Current row and prior source trails: Law 7/2025 articles 1 and 5, JETRO exact green-tea guide, personal-food registration exemption. Fresh current-law URL returned 403.
countries.finding: No new operative exception or complete commodity list obtained. The current-law risk qualification and previously verified JETRO processing-exemption possibility remain a real scope issue; neither a broad dead-plant definition nor absence of a named tea exemption resolves it.
countries.gap: An applicable published processing/risk exception or commodity condition covering this finished Japanese tea. A bespoke ruling is not inherently necessary; existing published general criteria could suffice if recovered. Receiving-emirate personal-food category remains as previously recorded.

countries.reviewedBasis: Saved 2017 Act definition and discretionary exemption evidence; complete saved 2019 German NPPO translation, especially sections 3–7, 9, 15 and 22.
countries.finding: Section 5(1)(6)–(7) requires the authority to publish allowed/prohibited commodity lists, but those lists are not supplied in the regulation. Section 22(2) automatic small personal exemption enumerates decorative plants/flowers and fruit, not all processed foods. Section 15(2) processed-wood-product relief concerns that material only. No general tea-processing or personal-post exemption established.
countries.gap: Applicable published allowed/regulated commodity or processing condition for manufactured tea under Article 3(7); missing lists could settle this without any new individual authority ruling. Separate 2025 food-law text remains a source gap.

countries.reviewedBasis: Complete NPPO-submitted 2003 GCC law and Bahrain pest-list annex; article 15 and 24 visual checks; current row food/permit scope.
countries.finding: Risk-based waiver power is not an automatic waiver. The complete attached list is a pest list, not a complete commodity restriction/exemption schedule. The personal exception concerns travellers.
countries.gap: Published article 15(3) commodity/processing waiver or sufficient local classification criteria applying to steamed/dried retail tea in post.

countries.reviewedBasis: Saved German NPPO consolidated 2012/2020 law: full definitions, articles 6–9 and 11.
countries.finding: Article 9(1) is unusually explicit about postal and non-agricultural-purpose materials, but waives only the certificate. Article 9(2) separately waives permits for seed samples. The separate biological-nature definition and article 7 permit duty cannot be skipped by using the certificate-only concession. No complete commodity or processing exception list appears in this text.
countries.gap: Evidence establishing whether steam manufacture changes the relevant biological nature for the statutory definition, or an applicable existing import-licence waiver for this tea. A non-agricultural-use certificate concession alone cannot close the route.

countries.gap: The operative ministerial list/decision for covered/exempt products under articles 3 and 8, plus ordinary personal-food clearance scope. An exhaustive current list could decide tea by inclusion/omission without a bespoke ruling, but was not recovered.
